note: MDC boat access on the Nishnabotna River just above its mouth on the Missouri. The primitive camping area is the north end of the gravel ramp lot and the small mown patch beside it, about 60 m back from the ramp; nothing built (no pads, tables, toilets or water). The river is in view down the open lot and ramp cut. On the river side of the levee, so it floods with the river. Gravel 160th Street in over the levee. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: MDC marks a Primitive Camping Area (map symbol + GIS point) at the head of the ramp lot - stays under the lot rule. Phone matches. Free/FCFS/14 nights/no hookups confirmed. Riverview stands (open lot and ramp between, ~60 m). Pin is on the gravel.
flags: LOT RULE - STAYS (designated point at a lot): the page lists 'Individual Campsites'; the 7/07 map legend has 'Primitive Camping Area' and draws the symbol inside a gravel loop with four short spurs north of the Parking Lot and Boat Ramp; GIS layer 27 has one 'Primitive Camping Area' point at 40.49942,-95.67704, 59 m north of the lot's GIS point. On imagery the 2007 loop and spurs are NOT there: the ground is one gravel lot about 60 m long and 15-20 m wide running north from the ramp head, and the camping point sits at its north end beside a mown grass patch of roughly 30 x 40 m. So in practice the camp is the far end of the ramp lot plus that grass - a designated point at a lot, which keeps it (as Lick Creek), not a built camp. No brochure PDF on the page.

WATERFRONT - RIVERVIEW STANDS: from the camping point the Nishnabotna (about 60 m wide here) is about 60-65 m south, down the open gravel lot and the ramp cut, with no timber in that line; to the west and south-west the bank is 50-60 m off across low weedy bottom with a clump of trees at the north-west. Nothing but the lot and ramp (day use) lies between, so it is a view, not on-water. Leaf-on imagery, one date.

FLOODING / ACCESS: the access is on the river side of the Missouri bottoms levee (the map draws the Levee 150 m east; imagery shows the levee road), so the whole 4 acres floods with the river; no closure is posted on the page now. 160th Street is gravel for 1 mile from Route BB and crosses the levee; no ford, no posted limit, no 4WD wording.
PIN: stored pin = the GIS camping point, on the north edge of the gravel. No move.
PHONE: stored 816-271-3100 matches the page's 'For more information call (816) 271-3100'.
